name: Jiang Zemin
role: General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party (1989-2002) and President of China (1993-2003)
summary: Jiang Zemin led the party and state through the 1990s on the line that the Communist Party must keep sole leadership while the economy opened to markets and foreign capital, with public ownership dominant. His 2001 'Three Represents' speech opened Party membership to private entrepreneurs; he defended one country, two systems, rejected Taiwan independence and Western-style political liberalization, and backed state control of the media and a strict family planning policy.

class-collaboration.rationale: His report calls for uniting people of all social strata, including private entrepreneurs, as builders of socialism, and Fewsmith's analysis of his July 2001 speech describes it as advocating that private entrepreneurs be allowed to join the Party.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: In a speech on foreign policy he says China will not enter into an alliance with any major power or group of countries, nor establish any military bloc, and that expanding military blocs and strengthening military alliances does not safeguard peace.

ethnic-nation.rationale: In his 1992 speech on ethnic work he describes China as a great family of ethnic groups with equal rights and calls for ethnic unity, opposing both discrimination and separatism.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: He says China cannot promise to renounce the use of force over Taiwan, that the question can be settled by peaceful or non-peaceful means, and that Taiwan independence will not be allowed.

free-trade.rationale: In his 16th Congress report he welcomes China's accession to the World Trade Organization as opening a new stage of opening up and says trade in goods, services and capital has grown markedly.

history-own-civilization.rationale: In the same speech he says all the people, especially youth, need to study the history of the motherland, particularly its modern history, as part of patriotic education.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: In his speech on military strategy he says China needs attack weapons and the necessary deterrence capability, including nuclear deterrence capability.

limit-population.rationale: He signed the Population and Family Planning Law (Order No. 63, 29 Dec 2001), which makes family planning a fundamental State policy to control the size of the population and keeps the policy of advocating one child per couple.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: In his 16th Congress report he asks for fuller play to the basic role of the market in allocating resources, while insisting that public ownership dominate and that the state hold controlling shares in lifeline enterprises.

minority-language-support.rationale: In his 1992 speech on ethnic work he says the oral and written languages of ethnic minorities are respected and preserved, citing over 200 newspapers and periodicals in minority languages.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: In his 16th Congress report he calls for upholding and improving the system of regional ethnic autonomy.

multipolar-world.rationale: In his 16th Congress report he says China is ready to work with the international community to boost world multipolarization.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: In his Tibet speech he says religion must not be allowed to interfere with political and social affairs such as administration, judicial proceedings and education.

one-party-rule.rationale: In his report to the 16th Party Congress he calls for upholding leadership by the Communist Party as a Cardinal Principle, with other parties only cooperating and consulting under its leadership.

party-commands-army.rationale: In his 1995 speech 'Uphold the Absolute Leadership of the Party over the Army' and in his 1989-90 speeches he calls that leadership the fundamental principle of army building.

party-controls-media.rationale: In his 1989 speeches he says some areas of the media are no longer under the control of the Party and the people and that departments must take decisive measures to correct this, and in 1996 he tells journalists to adhere to the Party's basic policies and principles on news reporting.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: In his 16th Congress report he says the Party must adhere to and improve democratic centralism, with members and organizations firmly carrying out the Party's line and decisions.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: In his 1990 speech 'Adopt a Marxist View of Women' he says the oppression of women is a social phenomenon that arose with private ownership and class divisions, though he treats it as something to be replaced by equality.

patriotic-education.rationale: In a 1990s speech he calls for broad and thorough patriotic education that must begin when children are small, with youth studying the history of the motherland.

property-fundamental.rationale: In his 16th Congress report he says the legal system for protecting private property should be improved, within a system where public ownership dominates.

public-ownership.rationale: In his 16th Congress report he says public ownership must play the dominant role, the state sector must be consolidated unswervingly and the state must hold controlling shares in lifeline enterprises.

region-keeps-system.rationale: In his 16th Congress report he affirms 'one country, two systems' for Hong Kong and Macao and offers it to Taiwan.

right-to-secede.rationale: In his 16th Congress report he says China's sovereignty and territorial integrity brook no division and firmly opposes all words and deeds aimed at 'Taiwan independence'.

separate-church-state.rationale: His Tibet speech invokes the principle of separation of church and state and bars religion from administration, courts and education, but he also has the state supervise and guide religious bodies and requires Party members to be atheists.

separated-powers.rationale: In his March 1990 speech on the people's congresses he endorses Deng Xiaoping's statement that China must adhere to the people's congress system instead of the separation of judicial, executive and legislative powers on the American pattern.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: In the same speech he says China will not yield to outside pressure or enter into an alliance with any major power or group of countries, nor establish any military bloc.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: In his Tibet speech he calls for tighter state supervision of lamaseries and lamas under government regulations, and in his 1998 Xinjiang speech for bringing religious activities into the orbit of the law and guiding religions to adapt to socialist society.

suppress-opposition.rationale: In 1989 he calls the spring protests counterrevolutionary rebellion stirred up by bourgeois liberalization and demands decisive measures against the spread of such liberalization.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: In the same speech he says women's liberation can be achieved only through the social liberation of all who are exploited and oppressed, and ties women's position to social and economic systems.

notes: A first audit. Answers rest on his own words: the 2002 Party Congress report, the 1989-1996 speeches in Selected Works volume I, and one UN statement. Volume II (1997-2002) was searched by theme and settles no further statement. His record (the 1999 ban on Falun Gong, the 1989 aftermath, the 1997 Hong Kong handover) was not used as a source because only secondary summaries were found; the answers that overlap it follow his words. Themes searched: government, economy, society, world, liberty, ecology, means.
